comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus every advisory-driven overrides entry, whose caret range is a security floor rather than a freshness range.
An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 — that script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions — so
nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file is what makes that check happen: on every run the script
executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to `expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different
means the condition that justified the pin has changed and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no
mechanical test exists — it is reported for manual review on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must
have an entry here, and every entry must correspond to a real pin; the script errors on either mismatch (rule G100).

fflate.why: GHSA-px8p-9vwx-vf98: fflate 0.7.0-0.7.4 unzipSync can loop forever on a malformed ZIP64 archive. Nothing here depends on fflate directly - satori pulls it in for font decompression and names it EXACTLY (fflate: 0.7.3), so no caret sweep can lift it, and satori@0.33.4 is its own latest release. npm audit fix would resolve it by downgrading satori to 0.32.0, which G100 forbids. The override forces a patched fflate on every copy in the tree. It is a caret rather than an exact pin so the sweep keeps floating it; the sweep took it to 0.8.x, past the 0.7 both satori and @shuding/opentype.js declare, and a full build regenerated dist/og.png through satori on 0.8.3, which is the one code path here that decompresses a font.
fflate.manualCheck: A changed value means satori moved off the vulnerable pin: if it now names 0.7.5 or later, drop this override and this entry.

typescript.why: Two independent consumers still refuse TypeScript 7. typescript-eslint (and its parser) peer-require >=4.8.4 <6.1.0, so type-aware ESLint cannot run on 7, and @astrojs/check — which backs `astro check` — peers ^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0 at its newest release, 0.9.10, so `npm install` fails outright with ERESOLVE on typescript@7. The caret sweep bumped ^6.0.3 to ^7.0.2 and broke the install; the pin is exact rather than ^6 precisely so the next sweep cannot drift it back to 7. Same rollback obsidian-dev-utils records for the same reason.
typescript.manualCheck: The mechanical check watches typescript-eslint only. @astrojs/check must widen too before this pin can be lifted — verify with `npm view @astrojs/check@latest peerDependencies`, which must accept ^7. When both allow 7, restore the caret range and run `npm run lint` plus `npm run build`.
